overall: The AG found the executive session purpose had expired and that the June 15, 2011 subcommittee minutes were incomplete, ordering release and reconstruction; the untimely deliberation claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged councilors were solicited to serve on a subcommittee as a preemptive strike against a tie vote, possibly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the allegation that the Council may have deliberated outside of a posted meeting is untimely, and therefore decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Council improperly refused to release the minutes of the June 15, 2011 executive session of the Contract Negotiating Subcommittee.
allegations.key_passage: Because the contract negotiation concluded when the full Council voted to accept the terms negotiated by the Subcommittee, the purpose for keeping the Subcommittee's minutes confidential has expired.

allegations.summary: On review, not raised by complainants: the Subcommittee stopped taking minutes during caucus sessions, leaving the June 15, 2011 executive session minutes incomplete.
allegations.key_passage: we found that the Subcommittee ceased taking minutes during caucus sessions, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints contained additional allegations the letter says fall outside the Open Meeting Law; the AG declined to investigate them.
allegations.key_passage: Additional allegations raised in the complaints are not covered by the Open Meeting Law, therefore we decline to investigate them.

remedy: Review and publicly release the Subcommittee's June 15, 2011 executive session minutes and any documents or exhibits used, unless the attorney-client privilege or a Public Records exemption applies.
Reconstruct the incomplete caucus portions of the June 15, 2011 minutes to the best of its ability and release them as part of the full executive session minutes.
remedy_passage: we find that the purpose for this executive session has expired and order the Council to review and publicly release those minutes and any documents or exhibits used at the executive session, unless the attorney-client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records law applies.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
